name: Our Lady of Sorrows
dates: Feast extended to the whole Church in 1814
history: The day after the Exaltation of the Cross, the Church stands with Mary beneath it. Simeon had told her that a sword would pierce her soul, and tradition counts seven sorrows, from his prophecy to the burial of her Son. Mary suffered with Christ, and her faith did not fail. The Servite friars did much to spread the devotion.
life: The seven sorrows traditionally honoured are the prophecy of Simeon, the flight into Egypt, the loss of the child Jesus in the Temple, the meeting with Jesus on the way to Calvary, the crucifixion, the taking down from the cross and the burial. Meditation on Mary’s compassion grew strongly in the Middle Ages, when the Stabat Mater was written, often attributed to the Franciscan Jacopone da Todi. The Order of Servants of Mary, founded in Florence in the thirteenth century by seven merchants, made the sorrows of Our Lady their particular devotion. Pius VII, on his return to Rome after captivity under Napoleon, extended the feast to the whole Church in 1814 in thanksgiving, and Pius X fixed it on 15 September. The Servite chaplet of the seven sorrows, seven groups of seven Hail Marys, is still widely prayed.
prayerTo: Holy Mother of Sorrows, you stood by the cross when others fled, and your faith held firm in the darkest hour. Stay beside all who keep watch at a deathbed, all parents who have lost a child, and all whose hearts are pierced. Pray for me, that I may stand by Christ in His suffering members. Amen.
penance: Pray the seven sorrows today, one Hail Mary for each, and visit, call or write to someone who is grieving.
meditation: Mary could not take away her Son’s suffering, but she stayed. Whose suffering are you being asked simply to stay beside?
prayer: O God, in Whose Passion the sword, according to the prophecy of blessed Simeon, pierced through the soul of Mary, the glorious Virgin and Mother, mercifully grant that we, who reverently commemorate her piercing through and her suffering, may, by the interceding glorious merits of all the saints faithfully standing by the Cross, obtain the abundant fruit of Your passion. Who livest…
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
